reader.requirement: At --std 85 argument-2 of ANNUITY must be an integer argument (A.2.2 type (4): an arithmetic expression that always results in an integer, so no numeric function per A.2.3 GR2) with a positive value; every such form (integer item, integer literal, integer function, always-integral expression) must be accepted and give the A.2.6.4 value, while a non-integer form may be refused; per A.1.2.2 and I.1.6 a violation's result is undefined, so refusal is permitted but not mandated. The witness covers literals, an integer item and an integer expression.

reader.notes: The integer screen is sound but not complete by design (kb/Work PB1526 records it fail-open): W-S * 3 over PIC 9V9 and (W-N + 1) / 2 compile and the 1.5 is truncated, the same at 2023. At 1985 this is permitted because §1985:I.1.6 makes the results of violating a rule undefined and A.2.2 AR4 leaves a non-complying argument's result undefined; every provably non-integral literal, item, numeric function and root quotient is refused.

refuter.evidence: Attack on the legal side (an always-integral form refused would be rejects-legal-source): rok.cob accepts and values PIC 9PP (=100) -> 0.01, SIGN LEADING SEPARATE S9 +3 -> 1/3, W-N / 1, W-N * 2 / 2, W-P2 / 4 (=25) -> 0.04, FUNCTION LENGTH (W-X) -> 0.25, FUNCTION ORD ("A") = 66 -> 0.015151515, qualified W-Q OF G2 -> 0.25, semicolon separator. rint.cob (rint-002): literal 2.0 -> 0.5, W-S * 10 over PIC 9V9 .4 -> 0.25, W-S - W-S + 5 -> 0.2, (W-N / 2) * 2 -> 1/3, W-N / W-N -> 1: all accepted. Refusal side (rbad-001): PIC P9 item, W-EL (1) / 2, FUNCTION RANDOM (numeric function, A.2.3 GR2) refused COBOL1627; index-name refused COBOL1637; BINARY-LONG refused COBOL0900. Class c: FUNCTION ABS (a 2002 function) as argument-2 refused COBOL1502 at 85 (rint-001). Fail-open acceptance of (W-N + 1) / 2 stays permitted by §1985:I.1.6. cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.2 AR4 'An arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value must be specified'; OK §1989:A.2.3 GR2 'A numeric function may not be referenced where an integer operand is required'; OK §1989:A.2.3 GR3 'An integer function can be referenced where an integer operand is required' (GR2 for this text fails cite.py; GR3 is right).
